bytes.q: Your app parses Claude's reply as JSON, and a stray sentence before the JSON breaks it about 1 in 50 times. What's the most robust fix?
options: Add "ONLY return JSON" in capitals to the prompt
Define a tool with a JSON schema and have Claude return the data as that tool's input
Raise the temperature so the model explores more formats
Strip everything before the first '{' with a regex
bytes.why: A tool's input_schema makes the structure a contract instead of a request. Prompt wording and regex cleanup only lower the failure rate; they don't remove it.

bytes.q: A long-running agent slows down and starts forgetting instructions. Most of its context is old tool results it no longer needs. What helps most?
options: Increase max_tokens
Clear or summarise stale tool results (compaction / context editing)
Repeat the system prompt in every user turn
Switch to a smaller model
bytes.why: max_tokens limits the output, not the input context. Removing or compacting stale tool output frees budget and keeps the important instructions prominent.

bytes.q: When does handing work to subagents pay off most?
options: Every task, because more agents are always better
Independent research branches whose raw output the main agent doesn't need to keep
Tightly coupled edits to the same file
Single-step lookups
bytes.why: Subagents shine at parallel, separable work. They return a condensed result and keep the orchestrator's context clean. Coupled edits create coordination conflicts.

bytes.q: Clickstream events arrive continuously. You need windowed aggregates in BigQuery within a minute, with minimal ops. Which pipeline fits?
options: Pub/Sub → Dataflow streaming → BigQuery
Cloud Storage → hourly Dataproc Spark job
A Cloud Function per event running a BigQuery INSERT
BigQuery scheduled query every 15 minutes
bytes.why: Dataflow is serverless and supports event-time windows and triggers on unbounded data. Per-event functions don't scale well for this, and the batch options miss the latency target.

bytes.q: Analysts always filter a 40 TB events table by event_date and often by customer_id. How do you cut query cost?
options: Partition by event_date and cluster by customer_id
Create one table per customer
Export to Cloud Storage and query as external tables
Add LIMIT 1000 to every query
bytes.why: Partition pruning skips whole dates and clustering reduces blocks scanned within a partition. LIMIT does not reduce the bytes billed.
